clauses.current_legal_basis: The U.S. Code release point 119-121 (current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted after that date and on or before 2026-10-14 are not reflected) prints the status line of EO 12163 as amended, which lists 'Ex. Ord. No. 12423, May 26, 1983, 48 F.R. 24025' among its amendments, in the note to 22 U.S.C. 2381. The bounded searches current-law:usc (2 hits), current-law:ecfr (0 hits; point-in-time as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (0 hits) located no instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes EO 12423, and no held later amendment of section 1-301(b) of EO 12163 exists.
clauses.reason: Section 1 amends section 1-301(b) of EO 12163 (Foreign Assistance Act functions of Part 1-3) by adding section 636(i) to the functions listed in that subsection. Per the owner's strike-and-insert ruling the amendment continues, as amended, while the parent stands. EO 12163 remains in force and its current U.S. Code status line lists EO 12423 as an amendment; no held later instrument rewrites 1-301(b) (later amendments touch subsections (a), (c) and (e) to (h) and the relettering by EO 13091 section 3 does not reach (b)); and EO 13637, the only held revocation linked by the dossier, revokes EO 11958, not EO 12163. Operative on 2026-10-14.

Section 2 amended section 1(d) of EO 11958 to delegate the functions under sections 22(a), 29 and 30 of the Act to the Secretary of Defense. EO 12560 section 11 (signed May 24, 1986; 51 FR 19159) restated 1(d) with the same delegation plus section 30A; under the strike-and-insert ruling that is an amendment recorded as a later event, and a human reviewer should note that the substance of the clause changed. The clause ended when section 4 of EO 13637 of March 8, 2013 (78 FR 16129) revoked EO 11958 of January 18, 1977 as amended. EO 13637 has no deferred-effect wording (its only 'effective' text is an unrelated statute title), so the revocation took effect on signing, 2013-03-08; the alternative reading is publication on March 13, 2013. EO 13637 section 1(d) re-delegates the same functions, so the delegation continues under that order, not under EO 12423.

research_rationale:
EO 12423 of May 26, 1983, Foreign Assistance and Arms Control (48 FR 24025, FR Doc. 83-14689; published May 31, 1983), was read in full from the held Federal Register text. It has two operative sections, both amendments of other orders: section 1 amends section 1-301(b) of EO 12163 by replacing the words 'and 635(g)' with a list that adds section 636(i); section 2 restates section 1(d) of EO 11958 as a delegation of the functions under sections 22(a), 29 and 30 of the Act to the Secretary of Defense. Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling (2026-10-21) an amendment clause continues, as amended, until the parent order ends. EO 12163 remains in force: its status line in the current U.S. Code lists EO 12423 as an amendment and the later amendments of EO 12163 held (EO 12458, 12560, 12639, 12680, 12738, 13091 and 13118) touch other subsections of section 1-301, none rewriting subsection (b), so section 1 is operative on 2026-10-14. EO 11958 was revoked as amended by section 4 of EO 13637 of March 8, 2013, with its substance re-delegated in section 1(d) of EO 13637, so section 2 ended on 2013-03-08. EO 12560 section 11 (May 24, 1986) earlier restated section 1(d) to add the functions under section 30A, which amends the clause (it adds section 30A) without ending it; the substance of the clause changed, which a human reviewer should note. The whole order is YES because section 1 is operative. No later event or clause is omitted: the dossier chain lists many other amenders of EO 12163 and EO 11958, which are not later events of EO 12423 unless they change 1-301(b) or 1(d), and EO 13637 does not name EO 12163.

savings.reason: Section 2's delegation to the Secretary of Defense of the functions under sections 22(a), 29, 30 and 30A of the Arms Export Control Act was carried forward when EO 11958 was revoked: section 1(d) of EO 13637 delegates the functions under sections 22(a), 29, 30 and 30A of the Act (22 U.S.C. 2762(a), 2769, 2770 and 2770a) to the Secretary of Defense, and section 4 of EO 13637 continues in force actions taken under EO 11958 to the extent consistent with it. The delegation thus survives under EO 13637 rather than under EO 12423 section 2.
